1. Cesto: múku odvážime. Všetky suroviny na cesto spojíme a miešame a miesime – ručne, robotom alebo v domácej pekárni –, kým nevznikne mäkké, hladké cesto.
2. Cesto preložíme do zľahka vymastenej misy, prikryjeme a necháme odpočívať asi 90 minút, kým nie je nadýchané, hoci nemusí zdvojnásobiť objem.
3. Plnka: v sotéze na strednom ohni zohrejeme olej.
4. Pridáme cibuľu a dusíme do sklovita.
5. Pridáme cesnak a mleté hovädzie mäso a opekáme 5 až 10 minút, pričom mäso pri hnednutí rozdrobujeme, kým nie je prepečené.
6. Plnku dochutíme soľou, korením a petržlenovou vňaťou, odstavíme z ohňa a necháme vychladnúť na izbovú teplotu.
7. Vmiešame syr. Plnku môžeme pripraviť vopred, zabaliť a do použitia uchovávať v chladničke.
8. Cesto rozdelíme na 16 rovnakých kúskov; ak máme váhu, každý bude vážiť asi 57 g.
9. Z kúskov vytvarujeme guľky a uložíme ich na zľahka vymastené alebo papierom na pečenie vystlané plechy asi 2,5 cm od seba.
10. Guľky prikryjeme a necháme odpočívať asi 15 minút.

11. Každú guľku sploštíme na placku s priemerom asi 13 cm, povrch potrieme trochou vajca rozšľahaného s vodou a doprostred každej placky dáme 2 PL (30 ml) plnky; dobre sa na to hodí naberačka na sušienky s objemom polievkovej lyžice.
12. Cesto pretiahneme cez plnku a dva protiľahlé okraje pevne stlačíme k sebe, aby sa plnka uzavrela; pirôžok by mal vyzerať ako knedlička.
13. Pirôžky uložíme na dva zľahka vymastené alebo papierom na pečenie vystlané plechy. Prikryjeme ich a necháme 1 hodinu kysnúť alebo kým nie sú nadýchané.
14. Ku koncu kysnutia rozohrejeme rúru na 205 °C (teplovzdušnú na 185 °C).
15. Pirôžky potrieme zvyšným vajcom. Pečieme 15 až 20 minút do zlatistohnedej farby. Nevadí, ak sa niektoré spoje roztvoria a plnka je vidieť; takto môžu byť ešte krajšie!
16. Pirôžky vyberieme z rúry a pred podávaním ich necháme 5 až 10 minút chladnúť.
17. Zvyšné pirôžky uchovávame v chladničke.

sk.v: Pakory sú najlepšie do hodiny od vyprážania.

en.t: 240 g chickpea flour
2 tsp (6 g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt; for table salt, use half as much by volume
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) ground red chile powder, such as Kashmiri
1/4 tsp (1.2 ml) ground turmeric
3/4 tsp (3.5 ml) chaat masala, divided
295 ml cold water
1 large head cauliflower, about 680 g, separated into bite-sized pieces, thick stems discarded
946 ml vegetable oil, for frying
Green chutney, for serving

sk.t: 240 g cíceková múka
2 ČL (6 g) hrubozrnná soľ Diamond Crystal (pri jemnej soli dáme objemovo polovicu)
½ ČL (2,5 ml) mleté červené čili, napr. kašmírske
¼ ČL (1,2 ml) mletá kurkuma
¾ ČL (3,5 ml) chaat masala, rozdelená na časti
295 ml voda, studená
1 veľká hlávka karfiolu (asi 680 g), rozobratá na kúsky do úst, bez hrubých stoniek
946 ml rastlinný olej, na vyprážanie
zelené čatní na podávanie

en.t: 1. In a large mixing bowl, whisk the chickpea flour, salt, red chile powder, turmeric, and 1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) of the chaat masala together. Whisk in the water until completely smooth. The batter should be runny like a custard and not too thick or thin. Fold the cauliflower florets into the batter to coat evenly.

2. In a 5680 ml Dutch oven or wok, heat oil over medium heat until it reaches 177 °C. Meanwhile, set a wire rack in a rimmed baking sheet. Line rack with a double layer of paper towels; set aside. Working in three batches to prevent crowding the oil, use your fingers or tongs to lift cauliflower from batter, allowing excess to drain off, then carefully lower into the oil. Fry on medium, stirring and turning pieces gently as they cook, until golden brown and crisp, 4 to 5 minutes. Using a slotted spoon or spider, transfer the fried florets to the prepared baking sheet and season with salt. Return oil to 177 °C and repeat twice more with remaining cauliflower florets. Sprinkle with remaining 1/4 tsp (1.2 ml) chaat masala. Serve hot.

sk.t: 1. Vo veľkej mise vymiešame metličkou cícerovú múku, soľ, mletú červenú čili papričku, kurkumu a 1/2 ČL (2,5 ml) chaat masaly. Metličkou vmiešame vodu, kým nie je cesto úplne hladké. Cesto by malo byť tekuté ako krém (custard), nie príliš husté ani riedke. Ružičky karfiolu zľahka vmiešame do cesta, aby sa rovnomerne obalili.

2. V liatinovom hrnci s objemom 5680 ml alebo vo woku rozohrejeme na strednom ohni olej, kým nedosiahne 177 °C. Medzitým do plechu s okrajom vložíme mriežku. Mriežku vystelieme dvojitou vrstvou papierových utierok; odložíme. Pracujeme v troch dávkach, aby olej nebol preplnený: prstami alebo kliešťami vyberáme karfiol z cesta, necháme prebytok odkvapkať a opatrne ho spustíme do oleja. Vyprážame na strednom ohni, pričom kúsky jemne miešame a obraciame, kým nie sú zlatistohnedé a chrumkavé, 4 až 5 minút. Dierovanou lyžicou alebo sieťkou preložíme vyprážané ružičky na pripravený plech a osolíme. Olej znova rozohrejeme na 177 °C a ešte dvakrát zopakujeme so zvyšnými ružičkami karfiolu. Posypeme zvyšnou 1/4 ČL (1,2 ml) chaat masaly. Podávame horúce.

en.t: 113 g seeded tamarind pulp
480 ml hot water
113 g jaggery or dark brown sugar
1/2 tsp (1.5 g) Diamond Crystal Kosher salt; for table salt, use half as much by volume
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) ground cumin
1/4 tsp (1.2 ml) ground Kashmiri red chile powder
480 ml water
113 g mint leaves
57 g cilantro leaves and tender stems
1 (2.5 cm) piece fresh ginger, peeled and thinly sliced
2 to 3 green Thai or Indian chiles, stem ends removed
1 tsp (5 ml) ground cumin
1 Diamond Crystal Kosher salt; for table salt, use half as much by volume
2 tsp (10 ml) chaat masala or store-bought pani puri masala
1 tsp (4 g) sugar (optional)
2 Russet potatoes (453 g total), peeled and cut into 5 cm pieces
1 tsp (3 g) Diamond Kosher salt; for table salt, use half as much by volume
2 tsp (10 ml) ground cumin
3/4 tsp (3.5 ml) ground Kashmiri red chile powder (optional)
202 g dried green mung beans or 1 1/2 cans chickpeas, drained (624 g)
3/4 tsp (2 g) Diamond Crystal Kosher salt; for table salt, use half as much by volume
4 dozen store-bought pani puri puffs (plus 1 dozen extra in case needed)
1/2 small white onion (85 g), minced
57 g picked cilantro leaves, minced (optional)
1 packet (200 g) plain or spiced bundi (deep fried chickpea paste balls), optional
1 packet (200 g) homemade or store-bought sev or bhujia (deep fried chickpea paste threads), optional
1. For the Sweet-Tart Spiced Water: In a large metal or glass bowl, cover tamarind with hot water. Soak for at least 2 and up to 4 hours.

2. Using your hands, press tamarind in the water to separate pulp. Set a fine-mesh strainer over a large bowl. Pour tamarind-water mixture through it, pushing and pressing on the pulp until all the water and pulp has passed through; discard seeds, skins, and fibres. Stir jaggery or brown sugar, salt, cumin, and red chile powder into tamarind water until well combined. Set aside until ready to serve, stirring occasionally to ensure all sugar and salt has fully dissolved.
3. For the Spicy Herb Water: In a blender jar, add 235 ml water, mint, cilantro, ginger, chiles, cumin, and salt and blend on high power until smooth, about 1 minute.
4. Add additional 235 ml water and blend for 30 seconds on high to ensure no lumps of ginger or chiles remain.

5. Set a clean fine-mesh strainer over a bowl, then strain blended puree through it, pressing on pulp to extract as much as possible; discard solids. Stir in chaat or pani puri masala. Season with salt to taste. The liquid should be spicy and minty. If it tastes too hot for your liking, stir in sugar; set aside until ready to serve.

6. For the Spiced Potatoes: In a medium saucepan, add potatoes, 1 tsp (5 ml) salt, and enough cold water to cover by 2.5 cm. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to a vigorous simmer over medium heat and cook until potatoes are tender, 12 to 15 minutes. Drain potatoes, transfer to a bowl, and let cool for 10 minutes. Mash potatoes roughly or cut them into 0.5 cm chunks. Stir in salt, cumin, and red chile powder, if using, until well combined. Transfer spiced potatoes to a serving bowl.

7. For the Beans: If using mung beans, pick through to remove any hard bits of debris, then rinse beans well. Soak mung beans in 480 ml of warm water, covered and at room temperature, for at least 8 and up to 12 hours.

8. Drain and rinse mung beans well and cover again with 475 ml warm water. Set aside until beans have softened, about 4 hours. Check if mung beans have softened by pressing one bean between thumb and forefinger. If it breaks easily, it is ready to cook, if not, continue to soak for 1 more hour and check again. Drain and rinse mung beans.

9. In a large saucepan, cover softened mung beans with 590 ml water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce heat to low and cook mung beans, uncovered, until beans are fully softened and break apart very easily when pressed, about 15 minutes. Drain and rinse beans and transfer to a serving bowl. Season with salt.

10. If using canned chickpeas, drain and rinse chickpeas before placing them in a mixing bowl. Using a potato masher or fork, mash chickpeas roughly. Stir in salt; transfer to serving bowl and set aside until ready to serve.

11. To Serve: Transfer the prepared sweet-tart spiced water, spicy herb water, spiced potatoes, prepared mung beans or chickpeas, onion, cilantro, bundi, sev or bhujia, and puris to separate plates and vessels on a serving table. Include a plate, a pair of teaspoons and a soup spoon per guest.

12. To Prepare 1 Pani Puri: The puri (puffed shell) has a thinner and crispier side; holding it on a plate, punch a roughly 2.5 cm hole into this thin side with your index finger, allowing the shards of puri to fall into the ball. Stuff the puri with potato mash and/or bean filling, then spoon sweet-tart spiced water and/or spicy mint water over top. Sprinkle with onion, cilantro, bundi (if using), and sev or bhujia (if using). Enjoy.

3. For the Spicy Herb Water: In a blender jar, add 235 ml water, mint, cilantro, ginger, chiles, cumin, and salt and blend on high power until smooth, about 1 minute.
4. Add additional 235 ml water and blend for 30 seconds on high to ensure no lumps of ginger or chiles remain.

5. Set a clean fine-mesh strainer over a bowl, then strain blended puree through it, pressing on pulp to extract as much as possible; discard solids. Stir in chaat or pani puri masala. Season with salt to taste. The liquid should be spicy and minty. If it tastes too hot for your liking, stir in sugar; set aside until ready to serve.

6. For the Spiced Potatoes: In a medium saucepan, add potatoes, 1 tsp (5 ml) salt, and enough cold water to cover by 2.5 cm. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to a vigorous simmer over medium heat and cook until potatoes are tender, 12 to 15 minutes. Drain potatoes, transfer to a bowl, and let cool for 10 minutes. Mash potatoes roughly or cut them into 0.5 cm chunks. Stir in salt, cumin, and red chile powder, if using, until well combined. Transfer spiced potatoes to a serving bowl.

7. For the Beans: If using mung beans, pick through to remove any hard bits of debris, then rinse beans well. Soak mung beans in 480 ml of warm water, covered and at room temperature, for at least 8 and up to 12 hours.

8. Drain and rinse mung beans well and cover again with 475 ml warm water. Set aside until beans have softened, about 4 hours. Check if mung beans have softened by pressing one bean between thumb and forefinger. If it breaks easily, it is ready to cook, if not, continue to soak for 1 more hour and check again. Drain and rinse mung beans.

9. In a large saucepan, cover softened mung beans with 590 ml water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce heat to low and cook mung beans, uncovered, until beans are fully softened and break apart very easily when pressed, about 15 minutes. Drain and rinse beans and transfer to a serving bowl. Season with salt.

10. If using canned chickpeas, drain and rinse chickpeas before placing them in a mixing bowl. Using a potato masher or fork, mash chickpeas roughly. Stir in salt; transfer to serving bowl and set aside until ready to serve.

11. To Serve: Transfer the prepared sweet-tart spiced water, spicy herb water, spiced potatoes, prepared mung beans or chickpeas, onion, cilantro, bundi, sev or bhujia, and puris to separate plates and vessels on a serving table. Include a plate, a pair of teaspoons and a soup spoon per guest.

12. To Prepare 1 Pani Puri: The puri (puffed shell) has a thinner and crispier side; holding it on a plate, punch a roughly 2.5 cm hole into this thin side with your index finger, allowing the shards of puri to fall into the ball. Stuff the puri with potato mash and/or bean filling, then spoon sweet-tart spiced water and/or spicy mint water over top. Sprinkle with onion, cilantro, bundi (if using), and sev or bhujia (if using). Enjoy.
1. Sladkokyslá korenená voda: vo veľkej kovovej alebo sklenenej mise zalejeme tamarind horúcou vodou. Namáčame aspoň 2 a najviac 4 hodiny.

2. Tamarind vo vode rukami stláčame, aby sa oddelila dužina. Nad veľkú misu položíme jemné sitko. Tamarindovú vodu prelejeme cez sitko a dužinu pretláčame a stláčame, kým neprejde všetka voda aj dužina; semienka, šupky a vlákna vyhodíme. Do tamarindovej vody vmiešame jaggery alebo hnedý cukor, soľ, rascu (kmín) a mletú červenú čili papričku, kým sa dobre nespoja. Do podávania odložíme a občas premiešame, aby sa všetok cukor a soľ úplne rozpustili.
3. Pikantná bylinková voda: do nádoby mixéra dáme 235 ml vody, mätu, koriandrovú vňať, zázvor, čili papričky, rascu (kmín) a soľ a na vysokom výkone mixujeme dohladka, asi 1 minútu.
4. Pridáme ďalších 235 ml vody a 30 sekúnd mixujeme na vysokom výkone, aby nezostali žiadne kúsky zázvoru ani čili.

5. Nad misu položíme čisté jemné sitko a pyré cezeň precedíme, pričom dužinu pritláčame, aby sme vytlačili čo najviac; pevné zvyšky vyhodíme. Vmiešame chaat alebo pani puri masalu. Podľa chuti osolíme. Tekutina by mala byť pikantná a mätová. Ak je na našu chuť príliš pálivá, vmiešame cukor; do podávania odložíme.

6. Korenené zemiaky: do stredného hrnca dáme zemiaky, 1 ČL (5 ml) soli a toľko studenej vody, aby ich prevyšovala o 2,5 cm. Na silnom ohni privedieme do varu, potom na strednom ohni stlmíme na výrazný mierny var a varíme, kým zemiaky nie sú mäkké, 12 až 15 minút. Zemiaky scedíme, preložíme do misy a necháme 10 minút chladnúť. Zemiaky nahrubo roztlačíme alebo nakrájame na kúsky veľké 0,5 cm. Vmiešame soľ, rascu (kmín) a mletú červenú čili papričku, ak ju používame, kým sa dobre nespoja. Korenené zemiaky preložíme do servírovacej misky.

7. Strukoviny: ak používame fazuľu mungo, prezrieme ju a odstránime tvrdé nečistoty, potom ju dobre opláchneme. Fazuľu mungo namočíme do 480 ml teplej vody a necháme ju prikrytú pri izbovej teplote aspoň 8 a najviac 12 hodín.

8. Fazuľu mungo scedíme, dobre opláchneme a znova zalejeme 475 ml teplej vody. Odložíme, kým fazuľa nezmäkne, asi 4 hodiny. Či fazuľa zmäkla, overíme stlačením jedného zrnka medzi palcom a ukazovákom. Ak sa ľahko rozpadne, je pripravená na varenie; ak nie, namáčame ju ešte 1 hodinu a znova skontrolujeme. Fazuľu mungo scedíme a opláchneme.

9. Vo veľkom hrnci zalejeme zmäknutú fazuľu mungo 590 ml vody. Na strednom ohni privedieme do varu, potom oheň stlmíme na mierny a fazuľu varíme bez pokrievky, kým nie je úplne mäkká a po stlačení sa veľmi ľahko rozpadá, asi 15 minút. Fazuľu scedíme, opláchneme a preložíme do servírovacej misky. Osolíme.

10. Ak používame cícer z konzervy, scedíme ho a opláchneme a potom ho dáme do misy. Štuchadlom alebo vidličkou cícer nahrubo roztlačíme. Vmiešame soľ; preložíme do servírovacej misky a do podávania odložíme.

11. Podávanie: pripravenú sladkokyslú korenenú vodu, pikantnú bylinkovú vodu, korenené zemiaky, pripravenú fazuľu mungo alebo cícer, cibuľu, koriandrovú vňať, bundi, sev alebo bhujiu a puri preložíme do samostatných tanierov a nádob na servírovací stôl. Pre každého hosťa pripravíme tanier, dvojicu čajových lyžičiek a polievkovú lyžicu.

12. Príprava 1 pani puri: puri (nafúknutá placka) má jednu stranu tenšiu a chrumkavejšiu; puri pridržíme na tanieri a ukazovákom do tejto tenkej strany prerazíme otvor s priemerom zhruba 2,5 cm, pričom úlomky puri necháme spadnúť dovnútra guľky. Puri naplníme zemiakovou kašou a/alebo strukovinovou plnkou a lyžicou zalejeme sladkokyslou korenenou vodou a/alebo pikantnou mätovou vodou. Posypeme cibuľou, koriandrovou vňaťou, bundi (ak ho používame) a sevom alebo bhujiou (ak ich používame). Dobrú chuť.

en.t: 1. In a large pot, combine potatoes, 3 tbsp (44 ml) salt, vinegar, and 1890 ml cold water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to maintain a steady simmer. Cook until potatoes are completely tender and offer little resistance when pierced with a paring knife, about 15 minutes. Strain potatoes and let drain, 1 to 2 minutes. Transfer to medium mixing bowl and set aside.

2. Meanwhile, combine breadcrumbs, potato starch, chaat masala, garam masala, Kashmiri chile powder, turmeric, and remaining 1 tsp (6 g) salt in a small mixing bowl. Using a fork or small whisk, stir until thoroughly combined.

3. Sprinkle spiced breadcrumb mixture and ginger evenly over still-hot drained potatoes in bowl. Using a potato masher or fork, mash potatoes roughly, breaking up any large pieces; do not overmash, as you want some smaller unmashed potato bits in the final mix. Add cilantro and chile and, using a spoon, stir potato mixture gently to distribute seasoning evenly; the mixture should be above 60 °C after mixing.

4. Using clean hands, roll 3 tbsp (44 ml) potato mixture into a ball between your palms, packing the mixture together much as you would a snowball. Flatten ball between the palms of your hands to form a puck, making sure that there are no cracks around the edges (if cracks are present, smooth edges with your fingers). Repeat with remaining potato mixture; you should have 15 potato patties. Let patties cool to room temperature, about 15 minutes. (Patties can be held at room temperature for up to 2 hours; refrigerating can cause the texture to become mealy).

5. Set a wire rack inside a rimmed baking sheet and line with paper towels. In a 25 cm cast iron skillet, heat 235 ml oil over medium heat until shimmering. Add 8 potato patties and cook, swirling occasionally, until golden brown on bottom, about 2 minutes. Using an offset or thin metal spatula, flip patties and continue to cook, swirling occasionally, until golden brown on second side, about 2 minutes. Transfer patties to prepared wire rack.
6. Add remaining 1 tbsp (15 ml) oil to skillet and repeat frying with remaining potato patties. Allow patties to cool slightly before serving, about 5 minutes.
7. Transfer potatoes patties to a serving platter and serve with mint and tamarind chutney alongside.

sk.t: 1. Vo veľkom hrnci spojíme zemiaky, 3 PL (44 ml) soli, ocot a 1890 ml studenej vody. Na silnom ohni privedieme do varu, potom oheň stlmíme, aby voda rovnomerne mierne vrela. Varíme, kým zemiaky nie sú úplne mäkké a pri prepichnutí nožíkom kladú len malý odpor, asi 15 minút. Zemiaky scedíme a necháme odkvapkať 1 až 2 minúty. Preložíme do strednej misy a odložíme.

2. Medzitým v malej miske spojíme strúhanku, zemiakový škrob, chaat masalu, garam masalu, kašmírsku čili papričku, kurkumu a zvyšnú 1 ČL (6 g) soli. Vidličkou alebo malou metličkou dôkladne premiešame.

3. Korenenú strúhankovú zmes a zázvor rovnomerne posypeme na ešte horúce scedené zemiaky v mise. Štuchadlom alebo vidličkou zemiaky nahrubo roztlačíme a rozdrobíme väčšie kúsky; neroztláčame ich príliš, v hotovej zmesi chceme mať aj menšie neroztlačené kúsky zemiakov. Pridáme koriandrovú vňať a čili a lyžicou jemne premiešame, aby sa koreniny rovnomerne rozložili; zmes by mala mať po premiešaní viac ako 60 °C.

4. Čistými rukami vyvaľkáme medzi dlaňami z 3 PL (44 ml) zemiakovej zmesi guľku a zmes pritom pevne stlačíme ako snehovú guľu. Guľku medzi dlaňami sploštíme na placku a dbáme, aby na okrajoch neboli praskliny (ak sú, okraje vyhladíme prstami). Zopakujeme so zvyšnou zemiakovou zmesou; mali by sme mať 15 zemiakových placiek. Placky necháme vychladnúť na izbovú teplotu, asi 15 minút. (Placky môžeme nechať pri izbovej teplote až 2 hodiny; v chladničke by mohli zmúčnatieť.)

5. Do plechu s okrajom vložíme mriežku a vystelieme ju papierovými utierkami. V liatinovej panvici s priemerom 25 cm zohrejeme na strednom ohni 235 ml oleja, kým sa nezačne vlniť. Pridáme 8 zemiakových placiek a za občasného krúženia panvicou opekáme, kým nie sú zospodu zlatistohnedé, asi 2 minúty. Zalomenou alebo tenkou kovovou obracačkou placky obrátime a za občasného krúženia opekáme ďalej, kým nie sú zlatistohnedé aj z druhej strany, asi 2 minúty. Placky preložíme na pripravenú mriežku.
6. Do panvice pridáme zvyšnú 1 PL (15 ml) oleja a zopakujeme so zvyšnými zemiakovými plackami. Pred podávaním necháme placky mierne vychladnúť, asi 5 minút.
7. Zemiakové placky preložíme na servírovací tanier a podávame s mätovým a tamarindovým čatní.

Placky necháme vychladnúť na izbovú teplotu, asi 15 minút. (Placky môžeme nechať pri izbovej teplote až 2 hodiny; v chladničke by mohli zmúčnatieť.)

5. Do plechu s okrajom vložíme mriežku a vystelieme ju papierovými utierkami. V liatinovej panvici s priemerom 25 cm zohrejeme na strednom ohni 235 ml oleja, kým sa nezačne vlniť. Pridáme 8 zemiakových placiek a za občasného krúženia panvicou opekáme, kým nie sú zospodu zlatistohnedé, asi 2 minúty. Zalomenou alebo tenkou kovovou obracačkou placky obrátime a za občasného krúženia opekáme ďalej, kým nie sú zlatistohnedé aj z druhej strany, asi 2 minúty. Placky preložíme na pripravenú mriežku.
6. Do panvice pridáme zvyšnú 1 PL (15 ml) oleja a zopakujeme so zvyšnými zemiakovými plackami. Pred podávaním necháme placky mierne vychladnúť, asi 5 minút.
7. Zemiakové placky preložíme na servírovací tanier a podávame s mätovým a tamarindovým čatní.

time.en: 35 min | Cook: 20 min | Total: 85 min

en.v: Food processor, cast iron pan or non-stick pan

sk.v: Kuchynský robot, liatinová alebo nepriľnavá panvica

en.t: 240 g all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting work surface
235 ml boiling water
Up to 59 ml toasted sesame seed oil
475 ml thinly sliced scallions
2 tbsp (30 ml) soy sauce
2 tbsp (30 ml) Chinkiang or rice wine vinegar
1 tbsp (15 ml) finely sliced scallion greens
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) grated fresh ginger
2 tsp (8 g) sugar
59 ml vegetable oil
Kosher salt

1. Place flour in bowl of food processor. With processor running, slowly drizzle in about 3/4 of the boiling water. Process for 15 seconds. If dough does not come together and ride around the blade, drizzle in more water a tbsp at a time until it just comes together. (Alternatively, in a large bowl add flour and 3/4 of the boiling water. Stir with a wooden spoon or chopsticks until dough comes together, adding water a tbsp at a time as needed.) Transfer to a floured work surface and knead a few times to form a smooth ball. Transfer to a bowl, cover with a damp towel or plastic wrap, and allow to rest for 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to overnight in the fridge.

2. Divide dough into four even pieces and shape each into a smooth ball. Working one ball at a time, roll out into a disk roughly 20 cm in diameter on a lightly floured surface. Using a pastry brush, paint a very thin layer of sesame oil over the top of the disk. Roll disk up like a jelly roll, then twist roll into a tight spiral, tucking the end underneath. Flatten gently with your hand, then re-roll into a 20 cm disk.

3. Paint with another layer of sesame oil, sprinkle with 120 ml scallions, and roll up like a jelly roll again. Twist into a spiral, flatten gently, and re-roll into an 18 cm disk. Repeat steps two and three with remaining dough balls.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together sauce ingredients and set aside at room temperature.

5. Heat oil in a 20 cm nonstick, carbon steel, or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully slip pancake into hot oil. Cook, shaking pan gently, until first side is an even golden brown (about 2 minutes). Carefully flip with tongs (be careful not to splash the oil), and continue to cook, shaking pan gently, until second side is an even golden brown (about 2 minutes longer). Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain. Season with salt and cut into 6 wedges. Repeat with remaining 3 pancakes. Serve immediately with dipping sauce.

1. Múku dáme do nádoby kuchynského robota. Za chodu robota pomaly prilejeme asi 3/4 vriacej vody. Mixujeme 15 sekúnd. Ak sa cesto nespojí a neobieha okolo noža, prilievame ďalšiu vodu po polievkovej lyžici, kým sa práve nespojí. (Prípadne vo veľkej mise spojíme múku a 3/4 vriacej vody. Miešame drevenou varechou alebo paličkami, kým sa cesto nespojí, a podľa potreby pridávame vodu po polievkovej lyžici.) Preložíme na pomúčenú pracovnú plochu a niekoľkokrát premiesime na hladkú guľu. Preložíme do misy, prikryjeme vlhkou utierkou alebo potravinovou fóliou a necháme odpočívať 30 minút pri izbovej teplote alebo až do druhého dňa v chladničke.

2. Cesto rozdelíme na štyri rovnaké kúsky a z každého vytvarujeme hladkú guľu. Spracúvame po jednej guli: na zľahka pomúčenej ploche ju rozvaľkáme na placku s priemerom zhruba 20 cm. Cukrárskym štetcom natrieme vrch placky veľmi tenkou vrstvou sezamového oleja. Placku zrolujeme ako roládu, potom roládu stočíme do pevnej špirály a koniec zastrčíme pod ňu. Rukou jemne sploštíme a znova rozvaľkáme na placku s priemerom 20 cm.

3. Natrieme ďalšou vrstvou sezamového oleja, posypeme 120 ml jarnej cibuľky a znova zrolujeme ako roládu. Stočíme do špirály, jemne sploštíme a znova rozvaľkáme na placku s priemerom 18 cm. Kroky dva a tri zopakujeme so zvyšnými guľami cesta.
4. V malej miske vymiešame metličkou suroviny na omáčku a odložíme pri izbovej teplote.

5. V nepriľnavej, oceľovej alebo liatinovej panvici s priemerom 20 cm zohrejeme na stredne silnom ohni olej, kým sa nezačne vlniť. Placku opatrne vsunieme do horúceho oleja. Opekáme a panvicou jemne potriasame, kým prvá strana nie je rovnomerne zlatistohnedá (asi 2 minúty). Opatrne obrátime kliešťami (dáme pozor, aby olej nešpliechal) a opekáme ďalej za jemného potriasania panvicou, kým aj druhá strana nie je rovnomerne zlatistohnedá (ešte asi 2 minúty). Preložíme na tanier vystlaný papierovými utierkami, aby odkvapkala. Osolíme a nakrájame na 6 dielov. Zopakujeme so zvyšnými 3 plackami. Hneď podávame s omáčkou na namáčanie.

en.t: 2 large bunches (about 350 g) scallions
90 g King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour
28 g cornstarch
1 tsp (4 g) granulated sugar
1/2 tsp (2 g) baking powder
rounded 1/2 tsp (3 g) table salt
227 g sparkling water, cold
about 6 tbsp (75 g) neutral oil, such as vegetable oil, for frying; divided
2 tbsp (28 g) soy sauce
1 tbsp (15 ml) rice wine vinegar
1 tsp (5 ml) toasted sesame oil
1 tsp (4 g) granulated sugar
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes)
1. Trim the root ends off the scallions and slice thinly on the bias; you should have between 710 and 945 ml of sliced scallions.

2. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, cornstarch, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Add the cold sparkling water and whisk to combine. Using a flexible spatula, fold in the scallions — it will look like a lot of scallions for the amount of batter.

3. In a medium nonstick skillet, heat 1 1/2 tbsp (22 ml) of the oil over medium heat until hot. Ladle about 120 ml of batter into the pan (a scone and muffin scoop works well here) and use a spatula or the back of a spoon to evenly spread the batter into a thin circle between 15 cm and 20 cm in diameter. Cook the pajeon until the bottom is golden brown and crispy, about 3 to 4 minutes.

4. Flip the pajeon and cook the other side until crispy, another 3 to 4 minutes. If necessary, turn the heat up towards the end of the cooking time to finish crisping the bottom. Transfer the pancake to a paper towel-lined cooling rack or plate, and cook the remaining batter, adding more oil between batches.
5. While the pajeon cook, make the dipping sauce: In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, and gochugaru. Serve with the pancakes.
6. Pajeon are best served immediately after cooking. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days; reheat in an oven or toaster oven on a wire rack set on a baking sheet.

c.t: Oil: 1–2 tbsp oil, sprayed or brushed on (instead of the frying oil)
Air fryer: 200 °C, 10–13 min per pancake, turning halfway (preheat 3 min with the tin inside)
Steps:
1. Make the batter as in steps 1–2. Put a 20 cm round cake tin that fits the basket in the air fryer and preheat for 3 minutes, then brush it with 1 tsp oil.
2. Pour in about 120 ml of batter, spread it thinly and air-fry until set and golden underneath, 6–8 minutes.

3. Turn the pancake with a spatula, brush the top with oil and cook until crisp, 4–5 minutes more. Repeat with the remaining batter and serve with the dipping sauce. The pancake is less crisp than when pan-fried.

time.en: 10 min | Cook: 15 min | Total: 40 min

en.t: 1 tbsp (15 ml) meaty dried shrimp
120 ml hot water
1 stalk lemongrass
53 g unsweetened dried coconut flakes
1 shallot, about 28 g, peeled and sliced thinly against the grain
2 (0.5 cm-thick) slices galangal, coarsely chopped
2 tbsp (30 ml) coarsely chopped peeled ginger
1 tsp (5 ml) shrimp paste
105 g packed grated palm sugar plus 71 g packed dark brown sugar (or substitute 140 g packed dark brown sugar)
1 tbsp (15 ml) fish sauce
59 ml water
2 tbsp (30 ml) finely chopped roasted peanuts
1 lime
1 (7.5 cm) piece fresh ginger, peeled and cut into 0.5 cm dice
2 shallots, about 28 g each, peeled and cut into 0.5 cm dice
71 g roasted peanuts
5 or 6 fresh bird’s eye chilies, sliced crosswise 0.5 cm thick
79 ml meaty dried shrimp
20 to 30 cha-phlu leaves or 7.5 cm squares collard green or Chinese broccoli leaves

1. To make the sauce, soak the dried shrimp in hot water for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, trim off and discard the leafy parts of the lemongrass stalk, remove the tough outer leaves of the bulb portion until the smooth, pale green core is exposed, and trim off the root end. Working from the root end, cut the bulb crosswise into paper-thin slices, stopping once you reach the point at which the purple rings disappear. Set the slices aside and discard the remainder.

2. Put the dried coconut flakes in a wok or 36 cm skillet and toast them on medium heat, stirring constantly, until medium brown, about 2 to 3 minutes. Reserve 2 tbsp (30 ml) of the toasted coconut flakes for the sauce and set the remainder aside for the salad. Wipe out any toasted coconut sediment from the wok. Add the lemongrass slices, shallot, galangal, and ginger to the clean wok, then toast over medium-high heat, stirring constantly, until fragrant and the shallot slices are dry to the touch, about 5 minutes. Place the toasted mixture, drained dried shrimp, and shrimp paste in a mortar or a mini chopper and grind to a smooth paste.

3. Put the prepared paste, sugars, fish sauce, and water in a 945 ml saucepan and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring constantly. When the sauce has thickened and reduced to about 235 ml, after 2 to 3 minutes, take the saucepan off the heat. Let the sauce cool completely. Once the dressing is cooled, stir in the chopped peanuts and the reserved 2 tbsp (30 ml) toasted coconut flakes and transfer to a small serving bowl.

4. To prepare the salad, quarter the lime lengthwise and trim away the core. Cut the quarters into 0.5 cm dice, leaving the rind intact. Alternatively, for those who are sensitive to the bitterness of the lime rind, cut the lime into wedges and invite diners to squeeze about 1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) lime juice onto each composed salad bite.
5. Arrange the lime, ginger, shallots, peanuts, chilies, dried shrimp, cha-phlu leaves, and the dressing on a large serving platter.

6. To eat, put a leaf on your palm, add a bit of each component to the center of the leaf, top with a small spoonful of dressing, gather up the corners of the leaf to form a bag, and eat the whole thing in one bite.
7. Note: If the diced ginger tastes too spicy hot, rinse it in cold water three or four times until the water runs clear and blot it dry.

1. Omáčka: sušené krevety namočíme na 15 minút do horúcej vody. Medzitým odrežeme a vyhodíme listovú časť stonky citrónovej trávy, z cibuľovitej časti odstránime tvrdé vonkajšie listy, kým sa neodkryje hladké, svetlozelené jadro, a odrežeme koreňový koniec. Od koreňového konca nakrájame cibuľovitú časť priečne na plátky tenké ako papier a prestaneme v mieste, kde zmiznú fialové krúžky. Plátky odložíme a zvyšok vyhodíme.

2. Sušené kokosové lupienky dáme do woku alebo panvice s priemerom 36 cm a za stáleho miešania ich pražíme na strednom ohni, kým nie sú stredne hnedé, asi 2 až 3 minúty. Odložíme si 2 PL (30 ml) opražených lupienkov na omáčku a zvyšok si necháme na šalát. Z woku vytrieme všetky zvyšky opraženého kokosu. Do čistého woku dáme plátky citrónovej trávy, šalotku, galangal a zázvor a za stáleho miešania pražíme na stredne silnom ohni, kým nezavoňajú a plátky šalotky nie sú na dotyk suché, asi 5 minút. Opraženú zmes, scedené sušené krevety a krevetovú pastu dáme do mažiara alebo malého sekáčika a rozotrieme na hladkú pastu.

3. Pripravenú pastu, cukry, rybaciu omáčku a vodu dáme do kastróla s objemom 945 ml a za stáleho miešania privedieme na stredne silnom ohni do varu. Keď omáčka zhustne a zredukuje sa zhruba na 235 ml, po 2 až 3 minútach, kastról odstavíme z ohňa. Omáčku necháme úplne vychladnúť. Do vychladnutého dresingu vmiešame nasekané arašidy a odložené 2 PL (30 ml) opražených kokosových lupienkov a preložíme do malej servírovacej misky.

4. Šalát: limetku pozdĺžne rozštvrtíme a odrežeme stred. Štvrtiny nakrájame na kocky veľké 0,5 cm aj so šupkou. Pre tých, ktorým prekáža horkosť limetkovej šupky, môžeme limetku nakrájať na mesiačiky a stolovníci si potom na každé poskladané sústo vytlačia asi 1/2 ČL (2,5 ml) limetkovej šťavy.
5. Limetku, zázvor, šalotku, arašidy, čili papričky, sušené krevety, listy cha-phlu a dresing rozložíme na veľký servírovací podnos.
6. Pri jedle si položíme list na dlaň, doprostred listu dáme trochu z každej zložky, navrch malú lyžičku dresingu, rohy listu zhrnieme do vrecúška a celé ho zjeme na jedno sústo.
7. Poznámka: ak je zázvor nakrájaný na kocky príliš pálivý, tri- až štyrikrát ho opláchneme studenou vodou, kým voda nie je číra, a osušíme ho.

src: Serious Eats — Jennifer Olvera — "Curried Jamaican Beef Patties Recipe"

time.en: 25 min | Cook: 50 min | Total: 135 min

en.v: Food processor, whisk, rolling pin, 15 cm round cookie cutter, rimmed baking sheet

sk.v: Kuchynský robot, metlička, valček na cesto, okrúhla vykrajovačka 15 cm, plech s okrajom

en.t: 360 g all-purpose flour
1/2 tsp (1.5 g) kosher salt
2 tbsp (30 ml) yellow curry powder, preferably Jamaican
turmeric powder
225 g cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
175 ml cold water
1 tbsp (15 ml) distilled white vinegar
1 large egg, lightly whisked
455 g ground beef
1 large yellow onion, finely chopped
1 Scotch bonnet pepper minced
2 medium cloves garlic, minced
295 ml low-sodium beef broth
1 1/2 tbsp (22 ml) Pickapeppa or steak sauce
1 1/2 tbsp (22 ml) Worcestershire sauce
1 tsp (5 ml) onion powder
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) cayenne pepper
1 tbsp (15 ml) yellow curry, preferably Jamaican
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) allspice
1 tsp (3 g) kosher salt
2 bay leaves
4 sprigs fresh thyme
56 g breadcrumbs
Egg wash made from 1 large egg beaten with 59 ml water
1. For the Dough: In the bowl of a food processor, pulse together flour, salt, curry powder, turmeric, and butter until butter is broken into pea-size pieces, about 10 pulses.

2. In a small bowl, whisk together water, vinegar, and egg. Add the mixture to food processor and pulse until dough is combined (will still look loose but should hold together when you ball up a bit in your hand). Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and shape into a 5 cm-thick disk. Wrap dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or up to overnight.

3. For the Filling: In a large sauté pan over medium-high heat, brown ground beef, breaking meat into little bits and stirring occasionally. When beef is nearly cooked through, about 6 minutes, reduce heat to medium and add onion, Scotch bonnet pepper, and garlic. Cook, stirring often, until vegetables have softened, 4 to 5 minutes.

4. Add broth, Pickapeppa sauce, Worcestershire sauce, onion powder, cayenne, curry, allspice, salt, bay leaves, and thyme to beef mixture in sauté pan, stirring to combine. Bring to a boil over high heat; reduce heat to medium low, and simmer, stirring occasionally, until most of the liquid has evaporated, about 12 minutes. Remove from heat. Discard bay leaves and thyme sprigs. Season with additional salt to taste, if needed. Add breadcrumbs and stir thoroughly.
5. Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat oven to 190 °C (fan 170 °C).

6. Flour your work surface and rolling pin. Roll out dough to a 0.5 cm thickness. Cut dough into 15 cm circles and place 2 heaping tbsp of meat filling onto half of each round of dough. Brush edges of dough with egg wash. Fold dough over filling to make a half-moon shape. Press edge with tines of a fork to seal. Brush tops lightly with remaining egg wash.
7. Set patties on a parchment paper-lined rimmed baking sheet and bake until dough is golden brown and cooked through, about 25 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

3. Plnka: vo veľkej sotéze na stredne silnom ohni opečieme mleté hovädzie mäso, pričom ho rozdrobujeme na malé kúsky a občas premiešame. 4. K mäsu v sotéze pridáme vývar, omáčku Pickapeppa, worcesterskú omáčku, cibuľový prášok, kajenské korenie, kari, nové korenie, soľ, bobkové listy a tymian a premiešame. Na silnom ohni privedieme do varu; oheň stlmíme na mierny až stredný a za občasného miešania dusíme, kým sa väčšina tekutiny neodparí, asi 12 minút. Odstavíme z ohňa. Bobkové listy a vetvičky tymianu vyhodíme. Ak treba, podľa chuti dosolíme. Pridáme strúhanku a dôkladne premiešame.
5. Rošt nastavíme do polohy pod stredom rúry a rúru rozohrejeme na 190 °C (teplovzdušnú na 170 °C).

6. Pracovnú plochu a valček poprášime múkou. Cesto rozvaľkáme na hrúbku 0,5 cm. Vykrojíme kruhy s priemerom 15 cm a na polovicu každého kruhu dáme 2 vrchovaté PL mäsovej plnky. Okraje cesta potrieme rozšľahaným vajcom. Cesto preložíme cez plnku na polmesiac. Okraj pritlačíme hrotmi vidličky, aby sa spojil. Vrch zľahka potrieme zvyšným vajcom.
7. Taštičky uložíme na plech s okrajom vystlaný papierom na pečenie a pečieme, kým cesto nie je zlatistohnedé a prepečené, asi 25 minút. Pred podávaním necháme 5 minút postáť.

en.v: The fritter mixture can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 2 days; let it stand for 30 minutes before frying.

sk.v: Zmes na krokety môžete uchovávať v chladničke v uzatvárateľnej nádobe až 2 dni; pred vyprážaním ju nechajte 30 minút postáť.

en.t: 455 g salt cod, checked for bones and rinsed thoroughly
340 g russet potatoes (about 2 small), peeled and cut into 2.5 cm chunks
4 tbsp (56 g) unsalted butter
3 medium garlic cloves, minced or pressed through a garlic press (about 1 tbsp (15 ml))
30 g unbleached all-purpose flour
120 ml whole or low-fat milk
59 ml extra-virgin olive oil
1 large egg, lightly beaten
1/8 tsp (0.5 g) baking powder
2 tbsp (30 ml) minced fresh parsley leaves
1/8 tsp (0.8 g) salt
1/8 tsp (0.6 ml) ground black pepper
945 ml–1420 ml vegetable oil, for frying
1 lemon, cut into wedges (for serving)

1. Submerge the salt cod in a large bowl of cool water; cover and refrigerate until the cod is soft enough to break apart easily with your fingers, about 24 hours, changing the water twice to rid the fish of excess salt.

2. Drain the salt cod, discarding the water. Place the salt cod and potato in a large saucepan and cover by 5 cm of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook until the cod and potatoes are tender, 15 to 20 minutes.

3. Meanwhile, melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk and cook, whisking constantly, until the béchamel is thickened and smooth, about 3 minutes. Set aside to cool slightly.

4. Drain the cod and potatoes thoroughly, then transfer to a large bowl. Using a fork, mash the cod and potatoes into small pieces. Stir in the béchamel, olive oil, egg, baking powder, parsley, salt, and pepper until well incorporated and the mixture has a creamy consistency. (At this point, the mixture can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Let stand for 30 minutes before frying.)

5. Adjust an oven rack to the middle position, place a large paper towel–lined plate on the rack, and heat the oven to 95 °C (fan 75 °C). Measure 7.5 cm of vegetable oil into a large Dutch oven and heat to 190 °C. (Use an instant-read thermometer that registers high temperatures or clip a candy/deep-fat thermometer onto the side of the pan.) Using two spoons, carefully scoop 12 golf ball–sized fritters into the hot oil. Fry, stirring to prevent them from sticking, until golden, about 6 minutes. Transfer the fritters to the plate in the oven using a wire spider or slotted spoon. Return the oil to 190 °C and repeat with the remaining cod mixture. Serve immediately with the lemon wedges.

1. Solenú tresku ponoríme do veľkej misy so studenou vodou; prikryjeme a necháme v chladničke, kým treska nie je taká mäkká, že sa dá ľahko rozobrať prstami, asi 24 hodín; vodu dvakrát vymeníme, aby sme z ryby odstránili prebytočnú soľ.

2. Tresku scedíme, vodu vylejeme. Tresku a zemiaky dáme do veľkého hrnca a zalejeme vodou tak, aby ich prevyšovala o 5 cm. Privedieme do varu, potom stlmíme na mierny var a varíme, kým treska aj zemiaky nie sú mäkké, 15 až 20 minút.

3. Medzitým v malom kastróliku roztopíme na strednom ohni maslo. Pridáme cesnak a opekáme, kým nezavoňia, asi 30 sekúnd. Metličkou vmiešame múku a 1 minútu ju opekáme. Za stáleho šľahania pomaly prilievame mlieko a varíme, kým bešamel nezhustne a nie je hladký, asi 3 minúty. Odložíme, aby mierne vychladol.

4. Tresku a zemiaky dôkladne scedíme a preložíme do veľkej misy. Vidličkou ich roztlačíme na malé kúsky. Vmiešame bešamel, olivový olej, vajce, prášok do pečiva, petržlenovú vňať, soľ a korenie, kým sa dobre nespoja a zmes nemá krémovú konzistenciu. (V tejto fáze môžeme zmes uchovávať v uzavretej nádobe v chladničke až 2 dni. Pred vyprážaním ju necháme 30 minút postáť.)

5. Rošt nastavíme do stredu rúry, položíme naň veľký tanier vystlaný papierovými utierkami a rúru rozohrejeme na 95 °C (teplovzdušnú na 75 °C). Do veľkého liatinového hrnca nalejeme 7,5 cm rastlinného oleja a rozohrejeme ho na 190 °C. (Použijeme vpichový teplomer, ktorý meria vysoké teploty, alebo na stenu hrnca pripneme teplomer na cukor/fritovanie.) Dvoma lyžicami opatrne vložíme do horúceho oleja 12 krokiet veľkosti golfovej loptičky. Vyprážame a miešame, aby sa neprilepili, do zlatista, asi 6 minút. Drôtenou sieťkou alebo dierovanou lyžicou preložíme krokety na tanier v rúre. Olej znova rozohrejeme na 190 °C a zopakujeme so zvyšnou treskovou zmesou. Hneď podávame s mesiačikmi citróna.

Steps:
1. Make the cod mixture as in steps 1–4 and chill it for 30 minutes so it is firm enough to shape.

3. Air-fry until golden, 10–12 minutes, turning carefully halfway. Serve with lemon wedges.

en.t: 110 g mayonnaise

1. **FOR THE SAUCE:**
2. Whisk 110 g mayonnaise, 2 tbsp (30 ml) prepared horseradish, 2 tbsp (30 ml) Dijon mustard, ¼ tsp (1.2 ml) cayenne pepper, and ¼ tsp (1.2 ml) pepper together in bowl; set aside.
3. **FOR THE ONION RINGS:**

4. Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 95 °C (fan 75 °C). Add 945 ml buttermilk to large bowl. Combine 945 ml all-purpose flour, 120 ml cornstarch, 2 tbsp (30 ml) Lawry's Seasoned Salt, 2 tbsp (30 ml) baking powder, 2 tsp (10 ml) pepper, and ½ tsp (2.5 ml) table salt in second large bowl. Transfer flour mixture to double-bagged large paper shopping bag.

5. Slice 2 peeled large onions (455 g each), crosswise into 1.5 cm-thick rounds. Reserve onion slices smaller than 5 cm in diameter for another use. Separate remaining onion rounds into rings. Toss one-third of onion rings in buttermilk to thoroughly coat. Shake off excess buttermilk and transfer onion rings to flour mixture in bag. Repeat with remaining onion rings in 2 batches. Roll top of bag to seal and shake vigorously to coat onion rings in flour mixture. Remove onion rings from bag, shaking off excess flour mixture, and transfer to rimmed baking sheet.

6. Transfer one-third of onion rings back to buttermilk and toss to thoroughly coat. Shake off excess buttermilk and transfer onion rings back to flour mixture in bag. Repeat with remaining onion rings in 2 batches. Roll top of bag to seal and shake vigorously to coat onion rings in flour mixture. Pour contents of bag onto sheet. Separate any onion rings that stick together.
7. Line second rimmed baking sheet with triple layer of paper towels. Add 2840 ml peanut oil to large Dutch oven until it measures about 5 cm deep and heat over medium-high heat to 190 °C.

8. Add one-third of onion rings to hot oil and fry, without stirring, until breading is just set, 30 to 60 seconds. Stir gently with tongs or spider skimmer and continue to fry until dark golden brown, 3 to 5 minutes longer, flipping onion rings occasionally and separating any that stick together. Adjust burner, if necessary, to maintain oil temperature between 165 and 190 °C. Transfer fried onion rings to paper towel-lined sheet and place in oven to keep warm.
9. Return oil to 190 °C and repeat with remaining onion rings in 2 batches. Serve onion rings with sauce.

1. Peel and slice the cucumber to yield 12 rounds that are each 0.5 cm thick. Reserve the unused cucumber for another use. In a small bowl, combine the vinegar, salt, sugar, and red pepper flakes. Add the sliced cucumbers to the vinegar mixture and toss to combine. Place in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.

2. Drain the cucumbers and pat dry with paper towels. Arrange the cucumber slices on a serving platter. Thinly slice one half of the avocado and divide the avocado among the cucumber slices—you can cut and shape the avocado so that they fit neatly across the cucumber rounds. 3. Melt 1 tbsp (14 g) of butter in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Carefully crack 4 to 6 of the quail eggs into the pan, making sure to keep the yolks intact. Cook the eggs until the whites are set, but the yolks are still runny, about 2 minutes. Using a thin spatula, transfer the fried eggs on top of the cucumber rounds. Melt the remaining tbsp of butter in the pan and repeat with the remaining eggs. Lightly season the eggs with salt and pepper and serve immediately.

1. Finely mince 4 garlic cloves and place in large bowl. Smash 4 cloves under the flat side of a knife and place in a large skillet. Thinly slice remaining four garlic cloves and set aside.
2. Add shrimp to bowl with minced garlic. Add 3 tbsp (44 ml) olive oil, 3/4 tsp (3.5 ml) kosher salt, and baking soda. Toss to combine thoroughly and set aside at room temperature.

3. Add shrimp shells to skillet with smashed garlic and add remaining olive oil and pepper flakes. Set over medium-low to low heat and cook, stirring and tossing occasionally, until shells are deep ruby red, garlic is pale golden brown, and oil is intensely aromatic, about 10 minutes. Oil should be gently bubbling the whole time. When ready, strain through a fine-mesh strainer into a small bowl, tossing and pressing the shrimp shells to extract as much oil as possible. Discard shells and garlic.

4. Return flavored oil to skillet and heat over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add sliced garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until pale golden brown, about 1 minute. Add shrimp and cook, tossing and stirring constantly until shrimp are barely cooked through, about 2 minutes. Add sherry vinegar and parsley and toss to combine. Season to taste with salt. Serve immediately.

1. **FOR THE DOUGH:**

2. Combine bulgur and water in bowl and let sit until grains begin to soften, 30 to 40 minutes. Drain bulgur well and transfer to bowl of food processor. Add lamb, onion, cinnamon, salt, and pepper and process to smooth paste, about 1 minute, scraping down sides of bowl as needed. Transfer dough to bowl, cover, and refrigerate until chilled, about 30 minutes.
3. **FOR THE FILLING:**

4. Heat oil in 30 cm skillet over medium-high heat until just smoking. Add lamb, ½ tsp (2.5 ml) salt, and ¼ tsp (1.2 ml) pepper and cook, breaking up meat with wooden spoon, until browned, 3 to 5 minutes. Using slotted spoon, transfer meat to paper towel–lined plate. Pour off all but 1 tbsp (15 ml) fat from skillet.

5. Add onion to fat left in skillet and cook over medium heat until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in pine nuts, cinnamon, and allspice and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Off heat, stir in lamb and pomegranate molasses and season with salt and pepper to taste.

6. Line rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and grease parchment. Pinch off and roll dough into 5 cm balls (16 balls total). Working with 1 dough ball at a time, use your lightly oiled hands to press and stretch dough into rough cup with 0.5 cm-thick sides. Spoon 1 tbsp (15 ml) filling into cup, pressing gently to pack filling, and pinch seam closed. Gently form kibbeh into 7.5 × 4 cm torpedo shape with tapered ends and transfer to prepared sheet. Cover and refrigerate kibbeh until firm, at least 30 minutes or up to 24 hours.

7. Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 95 °C (fan 75 °C). Set wire rack in second rimmed baking sheet and line with triple layer of paper towels. Heat oil in clean 30 cm skillet over medium-high heat to 190 °C. Fry half of kibbeh until deep golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Adjust burner, if necessary, to maintain oil temperature of 190 °C. Using slotted spoon, transfer kibbeh to prepared rack and keep warm in oven. Return oil to 190 °C and repeat with remaining kibbeh. Serve.

1. **NA CESTO:**

2. V mise spojíme bulgur a vodu a necháme postáť, kým zrná nezačnú mäknúť, 30 až 40 minút. Bulgur dobre scedíme a preložíme do nádoby kuchynského robota. 3. **NA PLNKU:**

4. V panvici s priemerom 30 cm zohrejeme na stredne silnom ohni olej, kým práve nezačne dymiť. Pridáme jahňacie mäso, ½ ČL (2,5 ml) soli a ¼ ČL (1,2 ml) korenia a opekáme, pričom mäso rozdrobujeme drevenou varechou, kým nezhnedne, 3 až 5 minút. Dierovanou lyžicou preložíme mäso na tanier vystlaný papierovými utierkami. Z panvice vylejeme všetok tuk okrem 1 PL (15 ml).

5. K tuku, ktorý zostal v panvici, pridáme cibuľu a na strednom ohni ju dusíme, kým nezmäkne, asi 5 minút. Vmiešame píniové oriešky, škoricu a nové korenie a opekáme, kým nezavoňajú, asi 30 sekúnd. Mimo ohňa vmiešame jahňacie mäso a granátovú melasu a podľa chuti osolíme a okoreníme.

Spracúvame po 1 guľke: zľahka naolejovanými rukami cesto pritláčame a naťahujeme do tvaru nepravidelnej misky so stenami hrubými 0,5 cm. Do misky naberieme 1 PL (15 ml) plnky, jemne ju natlačíme a spoj stlačíme, aby sa uzavrel. Kibbeh jemne vytvarujeme do tvaru torpéda s rozmermi 7,5 × 4 cm so zúženými koncami a preložíme na pripravený plech. Prikryjeme a kibbeh chladíme, kým nestuhnú, aspoň 30 minút alebo až 24 hodín.

1. Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 175 °C (fan 155 °C). Line rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. Process cheddar, flour, butter, salt, paprika, baking powder, and cayenne in food processor until mixture resembles wet sand, about 20 seconds. Add ice water and process until dough ball starts to form, about 25 seconds.

2. Turn out dough onto lightly floured counter. Knead briefly until dough fully comes together, 2 to 3 turns. Using your hands, pat dough into rough 10 cm square. Roll dough into 25 cm square, about 0.5 cm thick, flouring counter as needed to prevent sticking.
3. Position dough so 1 edge is parallel to edge of counter. Using rounded side of fork, drag tines across entire surface of dough to make decorative lines.

4. Using pizza cutter or chef's knife, trim away and discard outer 1.5 cm of dough to make neat square. Cut dough into 3 equal pieces perpendicular to decorative lines. Working with 1 section of dough at a time, cut into 1.5 cm-wide strips in direction of lines.

5. Evenly space cheese straws on prepared sheet, about 1.5 cm apart. Bake until edges of straws are light golden brown, 30 to 35 minutes, rotating sheet halfway through baking. Let straws cool completely on sheet. Serve. (Straws can be stored in airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week.)

src: King Arthur Baking — "Crunchy Parmesan Crackers"

time.en: 25 min | Cook: 16 min | Total: 67 min

en.t: 227 g King Arthur Golden Wheat Flour
1/2 tsp (3 g) table salt
a few grinds coarsely ground black pepper, optional
113 g Parmesan cheese, grated
8 tbsp (113 g) unsalted butter, cold
113 g milk, whole, 2%, or 1%
coarse salt, dried herbs, and/or grated Parmesan cheese, optional; for topping
1. Preheat the oven to 205 °C (fan 185 °C). Get out several large baking sheets; no need to grease them.
2. Whisk together the flour, salt, pepper, and Parmesan.
3. Add the cold butter, working it in until no large pieces remain; a mixer works well here.
4. With the mixer running (or stirring all the while), drizzle in milk until the dough comes together; you may not use the entire 120 ml.
5. Gather the dough into a ball, and squeeze it a few times to bring it together. Divide it into three pieces. If you have a scale, they'll weigh about 187 g each.

6. Working with one piece of dough at a time, flatten it into a rough square, and place it on a lightly floured work surface. Roll the dough 0.5 cm thick; it'll be about 25 cm square (or a 28 cm circle, if your rolling efforts result in a circle).

7. Transfer the dough to a piece of parchment or aluminum foil. Using a sharp knife, pizza cutter, or pastry wheel, cut the dough into 2.5 cm squares; don't separate them. You may trim the edges first, if you like, in order to separate the "good looking" crackers from the raggedy ones around the edges.
8. Lift the piece of parchment/crackers onto a baking sheet. Sprinkle the crackers with coarse sea salt, additional grated cheese, and/or dried herbs.
9. Repeat with the remaining pieces of dough.
10. Bake the crackers for about 15 minutes, until they're a medium golden brown. Remove them from the oven, and cool right on the pan.
11. When the crackers are cool, store them airtight at room temperature.

en.t: 120 ml popcorn kernels
1/2 tsp (2.5 ml) canola or vegetable oil
Kosher salt to taste
1. In a small mixing bowl, combine popcorn kernels, oil, and salt. Toss well until kernels are evenly coated in oil.

2. Transfer popcorn kernels to a clean brown paper lunch bag. Evenly fold top of bag over by approximately 4 cm and then fold each of the top corners of the bag over diagonally. Tear a small tab out of the center of each diagonal fold, and then fold that over as well. This prevents the bag from opening as the popcorn expands.

3. Place the kernel-filled brown paper bag in the microwave and run on high for about 2 minutes, watching carefully the entire time to ensure the bag doesn't smolder or, worse, catch fire. The exact timing will vary depending on the microwave, so be sure to err a little on the un-popped side of things to avoid scorching and burning the popcorn. Serve.
